operative_quotes.quote:
2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.
3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.
4. Divide the remaining shuffled deck into **4 roughly equal stacks**. Put End of Game **on top of the fourth stack**, then put the other three stacks above it. Place the resulting draw pile beside the board.

answers.answer: Each player gets two cards (in a two-player game, replace any F-lot setup card with a valid A–E card), places markers on those lots, and takes the sum of the two cards’ printed money values. Discard the cards to their matching color/Strip spaces. Shuffle the remaining deck into four roughly equal stacks; put End of Game atop the fourth stack, then place the other three stacks above it.

operative_quotes.quote: Each player rolls **2 dice**. The highest roller takes the player card and the first turn. After each turn, pass it to the player on the **left**.

Each normal turn has **Draw**, then **Play**: draw a property card, acquire its lot or die, pay every marked lot, pay money and score points for the indicated casinos, discard the card in its appropriate pile, then take actions in Play. Trading is also possible at any time, subject to the restrictions below.

answers.answer: Each player rolls two dice; the highest roller starts. After each turn, pass the player card left. A normal turn is Draw, resolving acquisition, lot income, indicated casino payouts and discard, followed by Play actions.

clauses: whether printed card starting money pays again

operative_quotes.quote: 1. **Draw a property card and take over its space before payouts.** If it is an empty lot, put your marker there. If it contains another player’s sprawled tile and die, replace their die with your own **at the same current pip value**, not the board’s printed value. If the tile has no die, add your die at the **printed board value**. If your own die already occupies it, leave it unchanged. The casino tile stays in place. Apply the dice/marker supply rules if necessary and settle any boss tie before paying casinos.

2. **All owned lots pay:** every lot with a marker pays its owner **$1 from the bank**, including the newly acquired lot, regardless of the card’s color or whose turn it is. Casino tiles do not also collect lot income.

Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.

answers.answer: The empty lot is acquired immediately when the card is drawn, before payouts. It pays its owner $1 from the bank during that draw’s payouts. Printed card money values apply only during setup and do not pay again.

clauses: what happens to the sprawled tile
what happens to the opponent’s die and its value

operative_quotes.quote: 1. **Draw a property card and take over its space before payouts.** If it is an empty lot, put your marker there. If it contains another player’s sprawled tile and die, replace their die with your own **at the same current pip value**, not the board’s printed value. If the tile has no die, add your die at the **printed board value**. If your own die already occupies it, leave it unchanged. The casino tile stays in place. 4. **Money:** each player receives **$1 per pip on each of their dice** in a paying casino, including players who are not its boss. **Points:** only the casino’s boss receives **1 point per tile** in that casino. Follow the scoring-break and separate-casino rules below.

answers.answer: The casino tile stays. Replace the opponent’s die with your own at its current value of 5, not the printed 2. On the imminent matching-color payout, you receive $5 for that die; the opponent no longer receives income from it.
evidence: Step 1 — Draw and pay, items 1 and 4

clauses: when same-color tiles form one casino

operative_quotes.quote:
A **casino** is one tile or an edge-connected group of same-color tiles on the same block. Same-color edge neighbors merge immediately into one casino, even if their dice belong to different players. Diagonal contact alone does not connect them; casinos cannot be subdivided after joining.

The **boss** is the player owning the **highest individual die** in that casino, not the most dice or the highest sum of pips. Several highest dice belonging to the same player are sufficient to make that player boss. Resolve highest ties between different players immediately as described under **Boss ties**.

answers.answer: Same-color tiles sharing an edge on the same block merge immediately into one casino. Diagonal contact does not connect them, and a joined casino cannot be subdivided. The boss is the owner of the highest individual die, not the owner of the most dice or the greatest total pip sum.

clauses: money paid to Red from its die
money paid to Blue from its dice

operative_quotes.quote: 2. **All owned lots pay:** every lot with a marker pays its owner **$1 from the bank**, including the newly acquired lot, regardless of the card’s color or whose turn it is. Casino tiles do not also collect lot income.

4. **Money:** each player receives **$1 per pip on each of their dice** in a paying casino, including players who are not its boss. **Points:** only the casino’s boss receives **1 point per tile** in that casino. Follow the scoring-break and separate-casino rules below.

answers.answer: Red receives $5 from its die plus $2 for its two marked lots, for $7 total. Blue receives $3 + $2 = $5. Red is boss with the highest die and receives 3 points for the three-tile casino; Blue receives 0 points.
evidence: Step 1 — Draw and pay, items 2 and 4

clauses: difference between Pay The Strip and color payout
eligibility of a casino with one Strip-adjacent tile

operative_quotes.quote: 3. **The indicated casinos pay money and points:** a single-color card pays every casino of that color anywhere on the board. A **Pay The Strip** card instead pays every casino with at least **one edge adjacent to The Strip**, regardless of color. A qualifying casino pays for **all its tiles**, not only the tile touching The Strip.

answers.answer: A color card pays every casino of its color anywhere. Pay The Strip pays casinos of any color that have at least one tile edge-adjacent to The Strip. If only one tile in a casino touches The Strip, the whole casino qualifies and all its tiles are included in the payout.

clauses: whether another player may act during your turn

operative_quotes.quote:
On your own turn you may **build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize and gamble** in **any order**, or stop taking actions. You may repeat actions except **gamble is limited to once per turn**, and **no die may be reorganized more than once per turn**. You must be able to pay the stated action cost. After each action check for boss ties and settle them before continuing.

No player may take an action on another player’s turn. Trading itself is not an action.

answers.answer: In Play you may build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize and gamble in any order, repeating actions subject to the limits: gamble at most once per turn, and no die may be reorganized more than once that turn. You must afford the cost and settle boss ties after each action. No one may take an action on another player’s turn.

operative_quotes.quote: Choose **a lot you own**. Take back its marker, choose an **available** casino tile of any color, pay the **price printed on the lot**, and place the tile there. Put one of your dice on it with the **lot’s printed die value** face up. Edge-connected same-color tiles merge immediately; boss control may change.

answers.answer: Pay $6, take back your marker, choose any color with an available tile, place that tile, and put one of your dice on it showing 2.

clauses: eligibility of opponent-marked or diagonal lots

operative_quotes.quote: You must be **boss of the casino** you expand. Choose an **empty, unowned lot sharing an edge** with it, pay **twice that lot’s printed price**, and place an available tile of the **same color** there. Put your die on it at the **lot’s printed die value**. You cannot sprawl into another player’s marked lot, your own marked lot, a built space or a merely diagonal neighbor. Without an available tile of the required color, you cannot sprawl.

answers.answer: As boss, pay $18 (twice $9), place an available gold tile and your die showing 3. You cannot sprawl onto an opponent’s marked lot or a lot that is only diagonally adjacent.

clauses: effect of merger with higher neighboring die

operative_quotes.quote:
You must be **boss**. Choose a **new color with enough available tiles for the entire casino**. Pay **$5 per tile** and replace **every tile** of that casino with the new color, returning the old tiles to their supply. Dice stay with their holdings and keep their values. You cannot remodel just part of a casino.

The result merges with any edge-connected casino of the new color. The highest individual die in the resulting casino determines the boss, so a remodel may hand control to another player; settle any cross-player highest tie immediately.

answers.answer: Only the casino’s boss may remodel it. For two tiles, choose a new color with at least two available tiles, pay $10, and replace both tiles; dice remain on their holdings at the same values. The remodel merges with any edge-connected casino of the new color. The highest individual die in the resulting casino controls, so the neighboring player’s higher die makes that player boss (settling any cross-player tie immediately).

clauses: which dice roll and who rolls
return locations and assignment of multiple dice

operative_quotes.quote:
You need **at least one die** in the casino; you **need not be boss** and may reorganize a casino containing only your dice.

1. Pay **$1 per pip on every die in that casino**, including opponents’ dice, using their values before the roll.
2. **Reroll all dice**, not a chosen subset. Each player rolls their own dice.
3. Each player puts their rerolled dice back on **their own original tiles**. If they have multiple dice, they choose how to assign the rolled values among those tiles; they cannot move onto another player’s former tile. Temporary markers can help remember the original holdings.

answers.answer: Yes. The non-boss may reorganize because they have a die there. They pay the total of all pips, including opponents’ dice: $5 + $3 + $2 = $10. All three dice reroll, each owner rolling their own dice. They return to their respective owners’ original tiles; an owner with multiple dice may assign the new values among those own original tiles.

clauses: whether free boss-tie rerolls are restricted

operative_quotes.quote: You may reorganize different casinos, but **no die can be reorganized twice during the same turn**. A casino containing **any die already reorganized that turn cannot be reorganized**, even after a merger into a larger casino. This limit applies to paid reorganization, **not free boss-tie rerolls**, which happen as often as necessary. Settle boss ties after the action.

answers.answer: No. The larger casino contains a die already reorganized that turn, so it cannot be reorganized this turn. Free boss-tie rerolls remain allowed as often as necessary; they are not barred by this paid-reorganization limit.

clauses: boss after both reroll below Green 4

operative_quotes.quote:
If **two or more players** tie for the **highest** value in a casino, reroll **all dice currently tied for highest**, **for free**. Leave smaller dice untouched. Reassess the highest value across the whole casino after each roll. If different players still tie for the current highest, reroll the current highest dice again. Continue until only **one player** owns the highest value; several highest dice belonging to that one player need no reroll.

A tie among smaller dice does nothing. If tied bosses roll below a previously smaller die, that unchanged die’s owner becomes boss. For example, Red 5 and Blue 5 reroll to 3 while Green 4 stays: Green becomes boss, without rerolling the 3s further.

answers.answer: Red 5 and Blue 5 reroll for free; smaller dice are left alone. If both become 3, Green 4 is highest and Green becomes boss. If all tied highest dice belong to one player, no reroll is needed. A tie among smaller dice has no effect.

operative_quotes.quote: **Once during your own turn**, choose a casino where **another player is boss**, and give that player the **House card**. If no opponent bosses a casino, you cannot gamble. You may bet no more than **all three limits**: **$5 per tile in that casino**, **your available money**, and **the boss’s available money**.

answers.answer: The limits are $20 (four tiles), your $18, and the boss’s $15, so the maximum bet is $15. Give the House card to the boss. You may gamble once during your turn.

clauses: outcomes for all two-dice sum groups
double payout limited by boss cash
whether stake is lost on a win

operative_quotes.quote:
Roll any **2 dice** and add them. The net transfer is:

| Dice sum | Result |
|---|---|
| 3, 4, 9, 10 or 11 | You win: the boss pays you **the bet amount**. You keep/get back your own stake. |
| 2 or 12 | You win double: the boss pays you **twice the bet**, limited to the money the boss actually has. You keep/get back your own stake. |
| 5, 6, 7 or 8 | You lose: pay **the bet amount** to the boss. |
The bank does not cover an unpaid portion of a doubled win in standard play.

answers.answer: With a $4 bet and a boss holding $7: sums 3, 4, 9, 10 or 11 pay you $4; sums 2 or 12 pay you $7 because the $8 double is limited by the boss’s $7; sums 5, 6, 7 or 8 make you pay $4. A winning bettor keeps or gets back their own stake; it is not lost. The bank does not cover the unpaid $1 of the doubled win.

clauses: what and when players may trade

operative_quotes.quote:
Players may trade **at any time, even off-turn**, except during boss-tie resolution or after End of Game is drawn. Multiple players may participate. Trade any combination of **money, lots, dice in casinos and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn**.

For a transferred lot replace the owner’s marker with the recipient’s marker. For a transferred casino die replace it with the recipient’s die, retaining the **current pip value**, not the board’s printed die. A die trade can therefore change the boss and cause an immediate highest tie.

You **cannot trade points or casino tiles**, or promise actions, exchanges or transfers for **future turns**. **No player can perform an action on another player’s turn.** A current-turn action can be part of a trade only for the player whose turn it is. If something prevents an element of a trade from happening, the subsequent steps of that trade do not occur.

answers.answer: Trades may occur at any time, including off-turn, except during boss-tie resolution and after End of Game is drawn. Players may trade money, lots, casino dice and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn. Transfer a lot by replacing its marker; transfer a casino die by replacing it with the recipient’s die at the same current pip value. Points, casino tiles and future-turn promises cannot be traded. No player may perform an action on another player’s turn; only the player whose turn it is can include a current-turn action.

clauses: result of each single casino award from score 8

operative_quotes.quote:
Record casino points by moving your chip on the **printed scoring track**. Numeric gaps are **breaks**: you must earn enough **from that individual casino** to reach the next printed value. Stop before a break you cannot cross and lose unusable excess points; do not save them for later.

For example, from **8**: an award of **1** leaves you on 8; **2 or 3** takes you to **10**; **4 or 5** takes you to **12**.

When several casinos pay you points on one turn, score them **individually, from smallest to largest**, choosing the order of equal-size casinos. You cannot combine their awards to cross a break. Several separate one-tile casinos therefore still cannot move a chip from 8 to 10.

answers.answer: From 8: 1 point leaves you at 8; 2 or 3 points takes you to 10; 4 or 5 points takes you to 12. Separate casino awards cannot be combined to cross a break, so two one-tile casinos cannot combine to move 8 to 10. Score casinos individually from smallest to largest, choosing the order when sizes are equal.

clauses: effect of End of Game draw on actions/trades

operative_quotes.quote:
As soon as anyone draws **End of Game**, the game ends immediately. Do not take Play actions or initiate trades after that draw. Make the **final payout for all owned lots and all casinos touching The Strip**, using normal money, boss-point and scoring-break rules. Highest score after that payout wins. If tied for most points, the tied player with **most money** wins. The source gives no further tiebreak if both remain equal.

In this base game, a player also **wins immediately at 90+ points**.

answers.answer: Drawing End of Game ends play immediately; take no Play actions and initiate no trades. Make a final payout for every owned lot and every casino touching The Strip under normal payout and scoring rules. Highest score wins; if tied, the tied player with the most money wins. The summary specifies no further tiebreak if money is also tied. A player also wins immediately upon reaching 90 or more points.

clauses: F cards during a turn and resulting payouts/draws
whether multiple payouts may occur before Play

operative_quotes.quote:
**Do not build on F block.** During setup, **discard any F-lot card and draw a replacement**; use the two accepted A–E cards for starting lots and money. Discarded F cards remain discarded.

During a turn, an **F-lot card places no marker**, but still causes the normal **owned-lot money and indicated casino money/points**. Discard it in its appropriate pile, then **repeat Draw** until an A, B, C, D or E card has been drawn and resolved. Only then proceed to Play. Thus multiple payouts can happen on one turn; you do not take actions between these draws. **End of Game still ends the game immediately** if drawn during this sequence.

answers.answer: In two-player setup, discard an F-lot card and draw a replacement; F cards remain discarded, and the two accepted A–E cards provide starting properties and money. Do not build on F. During a turn, an F card places no marker but still triggers normal lot and indicated casino payouts; discard it and repeat Draw until an A–E card is drawn and resolved, then Play. A turn can therefore have multiple payouts before actions, with no actions between those draws. End of Game still ends play immediately if drawn during the sequence.
